recorded: 2026-09-27, gfx1151 Strix Halo (zbook), Q4_K routed-expert prefill weight reuse
candidate: the Q4_K routed-expert gate/up projection joins the grouped-prefill route the Q5_1 down projection already took: one launch per (expert, out_col) that reads that expert's weight row once and reuses it across the expert's rows, instead of one launch per (out_col, lane) re-reading the whole expert weight matrix once per lane (hipengine/kernels/hip_gfx1100/quant/gguf_q4_k_gemv.{hip,py})
reason: the previous unit moved the Q5_1 down projection onto the reusing route and left the larger half of the prefill budget behind: attribution puts Q4_K gate/up at 53.40% of 512-token prefill kernel time against Q5_1 down's 31.40%. Q4_K's selected prefill reduces 128 lanes with reduce_block_sum(), so a grouped kernel that walks columns as `k = tid, tid + 128, ...` at the same 128 threads and reduces through that same tree is bit-exact against the incumbent rather than merely close - which is what makes the remaining 53.4% reachable at zero numerical cost.

mechanism.incumbent_reduction: gguf_q4_k_selected_prefill_out_kernel launches one block per (out_col, lane) with 128 threads and reduces each row with reduce_block_sum(): a 32-lane shfl_down tree per wave, then thread 0 summing the wave totals. The grouped kernel reproduces that association exactly at the same 128-thread k-stride, so it differs from the incumbent only in launch geometry.
mechanism.route: gemma4_project_experts_rows() tries, in order: the grouped family when the block has at least one compact row per expert and the quant key registers one, then the per-row selected GEMV, then the per-expert offset path. The route that ran is recorded in gemma4_moe_expert_route_counts(). No route code changed in this unit; registering the Q4_K family is the whole change.
mechanism.bit_exactness: the grouped kernel accumulates each row as `column = t, t + blockDim.x, ...` over the selected path's own thread count and reduces through its own tree, so grouped and selected outputs are bit-identical rather than within tolerance
mechanism.artifact_mix: the UD-Q4_K_XL file is not one quant: 29 of 30 layers are (gate/up Q4_K, down Q5_1) and layer 29 is (gate/up Q5_K, down Q8_0). With both families registered, 58 of the 60 expert projections per prefill block take the grouped route; the two layer-29 projections keep the per-lane pass because no grouped family is registered for Q5_K or Q8_0 with this ABI.

correctness.bit_exactness_test: tests/test_unit_gemma4_expert_route.py asserts bit-identical bf16 outputs between the grouped route and the selected GEMV at 10 quant/geometry cases: Q4_K at (out, in) = (1408, 2816), (2816, 2816), (64, 256), (37, 512), (16, 256) and Q5_1 at (2816, 704), (1408, 2816), (64, 128), (37, 96), (16, 32). (1408, 2816) is the artifact's own gate/up geometry. The geometries are per quant because Q4_K's block is 256 wide and cannot represent every shape Q5_1 can.
correctness.kernel_test: the same file checks each grouped kernel against a dequantized reference of its own quant with an empty expert in the middle of the expert list, so a kernel that shifted rows after an empty expert or ignored the compact row order fails
